# MosaiClusteR

> **An umbrella framework for multi-source and multi-omics clustering in
> R.** *One interface, many methods, and a complete workflow, from raw
> modalities to interpretable subgroups.*

**MosaiClusteR** (MoSaIC: **M**ulti-**O**mics **S**imilarity
**A**ggregation and **I**ntegrative **C**lustering in R) treats every
data modality (transcriptome, methylome, proteome, fingerprints,
targets, imaging, clinical) as one **tile** of a larger picture, and
assembles those tiles into a single coherent *mosaic* of sample
structure. It unifies a large family of integrative clustering
algorithms behind **one consistent list-of-matrices interface**, and
wraps them in a complete analysis framework: preprocessing, then
single-source baselines, then integration across five paradigms, then
evaluation and interpretation.

No single algorithm is best across all data regimes, so MosaiClusteR
gathers many methods on the same footing and gives you the tooling to
*choose between them*: cluster-number selection, agreement metrics,
visual comparison, cluster characterisation, and, for omics, pathway and
gene-set interpretation. It also introduces a **data-nugget
feature-weighting** scheme that offers a stable, big-data-friendly
alternative to variance weighting.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Why MosaiClusteR

Multi-omics and other multi-source studies measure the *same objects*
(patients, tumours, compounds, cells) through several heterogeneous
lenses. No single modality tells the whole story, and the many
integration algorithms in the literature live in scattered packages with
incompatible inputs and outputs. MosaiClusteR fixes this:

- **One input format.** Every method takes a `List` of matrices over the
  *same shared objects*, with **objects (samples) in rows and features
  in columns** (`n x m`), the same convention across the entire package,
  including the M-ABC family. Distance-matrix inputs (`type = "dist"`)
  are orientation-free.
- **One output contract.** Every method returns at least `DistM` (a
  dissimilarity matrix) and `Clust` (a hierarchical-clustering object),
  so results are directly comparable and composable.
- **Five paradigms, one roof.** Direct, similarity-based, graph-based,
  voting-based consensus, and hierarchy-based integration. Pick the
  right tool without leaving the package.
- **A full workflow, not only algorithms.** Normalisation, distances,
  partition extraction, agreement metrics (ARI, NMI, Jaccard), and
  method comparison are built in.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Installation

``` r

# the stable release, from CRAN
install.packages("MosaiClusteR")

# or the development version
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("lucp12891/MosaiClusteR")
```

MosaiClusteR ships C++ kernels for the M-ABC family, so a C/C++
toolchain is needed to build from source (on Windows install
[Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/); on macOS the
Xcode command-line tools). Every method has a pure-R fallback, so the
package still runs if a kernel is unavailable. A few methods rely on
*suggested* packages that are loaded only when you call them:

``` r

# optional, enables extra methods and distances
install.packages(c("SNFtool", "datanugget", "WCluster", "lsa", "analogue", "FactoMineR"))
```

| If you want                           | Install (Suggests)              |
|---------------------------------------|---------------------------------|
| Similarity Network Fusion (`SNF`)     | `SNFtool`                       |
| The reference data-nugget engine      | `datanugget`, `WCluster`        |
| Cosine, chi-squared, or MCA distances | `lsa`, `analogue`, `FactoMineR` |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 60-second quick start

``` r

library(MosaiClusteR)
data(mosaic_toy)                       # two sources, 60 shared objects, 3 planted groups
L     <- mosaic_toy$List               # a list of matrices, objects in rows
truth <- mosaic_toy$truth

## Integrate: every method shares one interface, so swapping it changes the paradigm
fit <- SNF(L, type = "data", distmeasure = c("euclidean", "euclidean"),
           normalize = c(FALSE, FALSE), method = list(NULL, NULL))

labels <- mosaic_labels(fit, k = 3)    # pull a flat partition from any fitted result
cluster_agreement(labels, truth)       # ARI, NMI, Jaccard, purity vs ground truth

## Same score from a different paradigm, e.g. a neighbourhood method
cluster_agreement(NEMO(L, k = 3)$cluster, truth)

## Compare two integrations directly
compare_clusterings(fit$DistM,
                    ADC(L, distmeasure = "euclidean", normalize = FALSE)$DistM, NC = 3)
```

That is the whole loop: integrate, extract, evaluate, compare. The same
three lines work for any of the methods below.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## The MoSaIC framework of use

MosaiClusteR is organised as a four-layer pipeline. You can enter at any
layer, and every layer speaks the same `List -> {DistM, Clust}`
language.

![The MoSaIC framework: a four-layer pipeline. (1) preprocessing with
Normalization() and Distance(), (2) single-source baselines, (3) the
integration engine spanning five paradigms, and (4) evaluation and
interpretation with mosaic_labels(), cluster_agreement() and
compare_clusterings().](reference/figures/framework.svg)

**Choosing a layer-3 method** (decision shortcut):

- *Want a fast, transparent baseline?* Use **Direct** (`ADC`) or
  **Weighted** (`WeightedClust`).
- *Sources are noisy and complementary, at genomic scale?* Use
  **Similarity** (`SNF`).
- *Want stability under resampling, from a resampling-based ensemble?*
  Use **Voting consensus** (`M_ABC`, `CEC`, `EvidenceAccumulation`).
- *Care about the hierarchy or dendrogram structure itself?* Use
  **Hierarchy** (`HEC`).
- *Have very large N or heavy-tailed data?* Set
  **`weighting = "nugget"`** inside the M-ABC family.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Method catalogue

> **Legend.** A named function is implemented in this package. A dagger
> (†) marks a method that needs an external graph-partitioning
> executable (METIS) or MATLAB, which is not bundled. A plain dash in
> the reference column marks methods that are interoperable with, or on
> the roadmap via, a reference package. All methods share the
> `List -> {DistM, Clust}` contract and take the same objects-in-rows
> input.

### 1. Direct clustering: combine first, then cluster

| Method | Function | What it does | When it is useful | Ref |
|----|----|----|----|----|
| **ADC** (Aggregated Data Clustering) | `ADC` | Concatenate all tiles into one wide matrix, then apply one distance and one hierarchy | Simplest baseline; when modalities are commensurate and you want a transparent reference | Fodeh 2013 |
| **ADEC** (Aggregated Data *Ensemble* Clustering) | `ADEC` | ADC plus resampling of features and cut-points to a co-clustering matrix | When ADC is unstable and you want a stability layer | Fodeh 2013 |

### 2. Similarity-based: fuse object-by-object similarity

| Method | Function | What it does | When it is useful | Ref |
|----|----|----|----|----|
| **Weighted Clustering** | `WeightedClust` | Convex combination `sum(wk Dk)` over a weight grid | When you want to tune and inspect the trade-off between sources | Perualila-Tan 2016 |
| **SNF** (Similarity Network Fusion) | `SNF` | Cross-diffuse per-source similarity networks into one fused network | Noisy, complementary, genomic-scale sources; the multi-omics workhorse | Wang 2014 |
| **WonM** (Weighting on Membership) | `WonM` | Consensus co-membership across many cut-points *k* | When you do not want to commit to a single *k* | \- |
| **NEMO** (Neighborhood-based Multi-Omics) | `NEMO` | Locally-scaled kNN affinities averaged over the omics measuring each pair, then spectral clustering | When samples are **missing some modalities** (no imputation needed) | Rappoport 2019 |
| **Spectral clustering** | `spectral_clustering` | Normalised-Laplacian embedding plus k-means on any affinity | Final clusterer for fused or similarity matrices (SNF, NEMO, Spectrum) | Ng 2002 |
| **ab-SNF** | \- | SNF with association or variance feature weights | When a few features carry the signal and should drive the network | Zhang 2022 |
| **CIMLR / rMKL-LPP** | \- | Multi-kernel similarity learning | Many heterogeneous kernels; learn their weights | Zhang 2022 |

### 3. Graph-based: partition an ensemble (hyper)graph

| Method | Function | What it does | When it is useful | Ref |
|----|----|----|----|----|
| **CSPA / HGPA / MCLA** | `EnsembleClustering` † | Cluster-ensemble via (hyper)graph partitioning | Combining many base partitions into one stable consensus | Strehl 2002 |
| **HBGF** (Hybrid Bipartite Graph Formulation) | `HBGF` | Partition an object-to-cluster bipartite graph (SVD plus k-means) | Ensembles where objects and clusters co-embed naturally | Fern 2004 |
| **Clustering Aggregation** (Balls / Agglo / Furthest) | `ClusteringAggregation` | Minimise pairwise disagreement cost | When you have several partitions and want the median one | Gionis 2007 |

### 4. Voting-based consensus: let partitions vote

| Method | Function | What it does | When it is useful | Ref |
|----|----|----|----|----|
| **M-ABC** (Multi-source Aggregating Bundles of Clusters) | `M_ABC` | Per-source bootstrap of *feature bundles* to a consensus co-clustering dissimilarity | High-dimensional sources, where signal hides in feature subsets; stable under resampling; supports **data-nugget weighting** | Amaratunga 2008 |
| **M-ABCdist** | `M_ABCdist` | M-ABC that accumulates *distances* (keeps geometry), then fuses | When you want continuous dissimilarities rather than co-clustering counts | Amaratunga 2008 |
| **M-ABCdeep** (deep-learning ABC) | `M_ABCdeep` / `ABCdeep.SingleInMultiple` | M-ABC whose base clustering is a neural autoencoder embedding plus latent clustering; self-contained R network, no Python or torch | Nonlinear or complex per-source structure; when a learned embedding beats a raw distance | Amaratunga 2008 |
| **CEC** ((Consensus) Ensemble Clustering) | `CEC` | Incidence accumulation across sources and cut-points | A solid, weight-aware consensus baseline | Fodeh 2013 |
| **CVAA / W-CVAA** | `CVAA` | Cumulative voting aggregation (and weighted) | Aligning and merging many partitions by voting | Saeed 2012/2014 |
| **IVC / IPVC / IPC** | `ConsensusClustering` | Iterative (probabilistic) voting consensus | Iteratively refine a consensus labelling | Nguyen 2007 |
| **EA** (Evidence Accumulation) | `EvidenceAccumulation` | Co-association matrix across partitions (SL / SL-agnes / MST) | Classic, parameter-light consensus | Fred 2005 |
| **CTS / SRS / ASRS** | `LinkBasedClustering` | Link-based cluster ensembles (CTS and SRS pure-R; ASRS needs MATLAB) | When pairwise *link* similarity refines the consensus | Iam-On 2010 |

### 5. Hierarchy-based: consense the trees themselves

| Method | Function | What it does | When it is useful | Ref |
|----|----|----|----|----|
| **HEC** (Hierarchical Ensemble Clustering) | `HierarchicalEnsembleClustering` | Aggregate cophenetic distances to the closest ultrametric (Floyd-Warshall) | When the *dendrogram structure* across sources is the object of interest | Zheng 2014 |
| **EHC** (Ensemble for Hierarchical Clustering) | `EHC` † | Graph aggregation of dendrogram association strengths | Graph-flavoured hierarchical consensus | Hossain 2012 |

### 6. Model-based and factor integration

| Method | Function | What it does | When it is useful | Ref |
|----|----|----|----|----|
| **intNMF** (integrative NMF) | `intNMF` | Shared non-negative basis `W` plus per-omic `Hk`; consensus clustering of `W` | Low-rank, parts-based integration; non-negative data | Chalise 2017 |
| **LUCID** | `LUCID` ‡ | Latent clusters jointly from exposures, omics **and** an outcome (quasi-mediation, EM) | Supervised subtyping where an outcome should shape the clusters | Zhao 2024 |
| **iCluster / iClusterPlus / iClusterBayes** | \- | Joint latent-variable integration, mixed data types, feature selection | Zhang 2022 |  |
| **moCluster / MOFA / JIVE** | \- | Low-rank or factor decomposition of shared and individual variation | Zhang 2022 |  |

‡ `LUCID` wraps the **LUCIDus** package (a *Suggests* dependency).

### Data reduction and weighting

| Tool | Function | Role |
|----|----|----|
| **Data nuggets** | `create_data_nuggets`, `nugget_feature_weights` | Compress N observations into M weighted representatives; derive stable **feature weights** for M-ABC |
| **Data-nugget clustering** | `nugget_cluster`, `Wkmeans`, `Whclust` | Cluster the compressed representatives directly (weighted k-means or weighted Ward), then map back to objects, for big-data clustering |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Spotlight: M-ABC and data nuggets

**M-ABC** generalises the single-source *Aggregating Bundles of
Clusters* algorithm (Amaratunga et al. 2008) to many heterogeneous
sources. For each source it repeats, `numsim` times: bootstrap the
samples, draw a **weighted subsample of features**, cluster, and record
co-clustering. Per-source evidence is accumulated into one consensus
dissimilarity, then clustered.

The feature subsample is the heart of the method, and *how features are
weighted* matters:

| `weighting` | Score behind the selection probability | Best when |
|----|----|----|
| `"var"` | feature **variance** (classic) | signal lives in high-variance features |
| `"cv"` | coefficient of variation | scale-free relative dispersion |
| `"nugget"` | **data-nugget between-group weighted variance** | large N, heavy tails, outliers: signal that resists noise |
| `"equal"` | flat | ablation or no prior |

**Why data nuggets?** A data nugget summarises a group of observations
by a *centre*, a *weight* (how many observations it represents) and a
*scale* (its internal spread). Building nuggets over the samples and
asking *which features separate the nugget centres* yields a
feature-importance score that rewards real between-group signal while
discounting within-nugget noise, and it scales to very large N because
it works on `M` representatives with `M` far below `N`.

``` r

# Inspect the nugget compression and the weights it induces
# (objects are in rows, so pass the source directly: no transpose)
dn <- create_data_nuggets(L[[1]], max_nuggets = 25)
dn                                   # 60 obs -> up to 25 nuggets (reduction reported)
w  <- nugget_feature_weights(dn, type = "between")   # stable feature weights

# Drop straight into M-ABC
M_ABC(L, weighting = c("nugget", "nugget"),
      nugget_args = list(max_nuggets = 25, seed = 1))
```

If the reference `datanugget` package is installed you can swap in its
engine with `create_data_nuggets(x, engine = "datanugget")`; otherwise
the built-in native engine is used (no extra dependency).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Evaluation and comparison toolkit

``` r

mosaic_labels(fit, k = 3)                 # extract a partition from any result
cluster_agreement(a, b)                   # ARI, NMI, pairwise Jaccard
compare_clusterings(D1, D2, NC = 3)       # cluster two dissimilarities and compare
```

[`cluster_agreement()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/cluster_agreement.md)
rule of thumb (ARI): above 0.90 excellent, 0.75 to 0.90 good, 0.50 to
0.75 moderate, below 0.50 weak.

### Downstream analysis and visualisation

The package also ships a full downstream analysis suite (Layer 4). These
guard their heavier dependencies via *Suggests* and raise an informative
error if one is missing.

| Purpose | Functions | Needs |
|----|----|----|
| Cross-method comparison | `ReorderToReference`, `SimilarityMeasure`, `CompareSilCluster`, `CompareSvsM`, `CompareInteractive`, `SelectnrClusters` | base / `plotrix` |
| Source weighting | `DetermineWeight_SilClust`, `DetermineWeight_SimClust` | base |
| Cluster navigation | `FindCluster`, `FindElement`, `SharedComps`, `TrackCluster`, `ChooseCluster` | base |
| Characterisation | `CharacteristicFeatures`, `FeatSelection`, `FeaturesOfCluster` | base |
| Dendrograms and colours | `ComparePlot`, `Cyclogram`, `ClusterPlot`, `ColorPalette`, `LabelPlot` | `circlize`, `plotrix` |
| Heatmaps and boxplots | `HeatmapPlot`, `HeatmapSelection`, `SimilarityHeatmap`, `BoxPlotDistance` | `gplots`, `ggplot2`, `gridExtra` |
| Feature and profile plots | `BinFeaturesPlot_SingleData`, `BinFeaturesPlot_MultipleData`, `ContFeaturesPlot`, `ProfilePlot` | `plotrix`, `Biobase` |
| Differential expression | `DiffGenes`, `DiffGenesSelection`, `FindGenes` | `limma` |
| Pathway analysis | `PathwayAnalysis`, `Pathways`, `PathwaysIter`, `PathwaysSelection`, `PreparePathway`, `PlotPathways`, `Geneset.intersect` | `MLP`, `biomaRt`, `org.Hs.eg.db` |
| Shared genes, paths, features | `SharedGenesPathsFeat`, `SharedSelection`, `SharedSelectionLimma`, `SharedSelectionMLP` | base / `limma` / `MLP` |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Datasets

- **`mosaic_toy`**: a bundled two-source example (60 shared samples, 3
  planted groups) for instant experimentation and the test suite.
- **[`mosaic_sim()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/mosaic_sim.md)**:
  generate your own multi-source data with controllable group structure,
  informative-feature counts and effect size.

The methods are designed for, and have been evaluated on, multi-omics
benchmarks in the spirit of the **LUCIDus** simulated-HELIX data,
**TCGA** subtype cohorts, and the **MCF7** compound, fingerprint and
transcriptome panel used in the companion manuscript.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Design principles

1.  **Source-agnostic.** Methods do not care whether a tile is RNA,
    methylation, fingerprints or clinical scores.
2.  **Composable.** A uniform `{DistM, Clust}` return makes any two
    methods comparable and any result re-usable.
3.  **Honest dependencies.** The core is pure R; heavyweight methods
    degrade gracefully when an optional package is absent.
4.  **Tested.** A `testthat` suite covers the data-nugget engine, every
    weighting scheme, the M-ABC family, distances and metrics.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Package index

## Preprocessing

Make heterogeneous sources comparable and turn a source into a
dissimilarity.

- [`Normalization()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/Normalization.md)
  : Normalisation of features
- [`Distance()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/Distance.md)
  [`Distance_v2()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/Distance.md)
  : Compute a distance matrix
- [`SimilarityMeasure()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/SimilarityMeasure.md)
  : Similarity of a set of clusterings to a reference
- [`Cluster()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/Cluster.md)
  : Single-source base clustering

## Integration — Direct

Concatenate the sources and cluster once.

- [`ADC()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/ADC.md) :
  Aggregated data clustering
- [`ADEC()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/ADEC.md)
  : Aggregated data ensemble clustering

## Integration — Similarity-based

Combine per-source object similarities.

- [`WeightedClust()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/WeightedClust.md)
  : Weighted clustering
- [`WonM()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/WonM.md)
  : Weighting on Membership clustering
- [`SNF()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/SNF.md) :
  Similarity network fusion
- [`NEMO()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/NEMO.md)
  : NEMO: neighborhood-based multi-omics clustering

## Integration — Graph-based

Partition a graph built from many clusterings.

- [`EnsembleClustering()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/EnsembleClustering.md)
  : Ensemble clustering via graph partitioning (CSPA / HGPA / MCLA)
- [`HBGF()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/HBGF.md)
  : Hybrid Bipartite Graph Formulation
- [`ClusteringAggregation()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/ClusteringAggregation.md)
  : Clustering aggregation

## Integration — Voting / consensus

Let many partitions vote on co-membership, including the ABC family.

- [`CEC()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/CEC.md) :
  Complementary ensemble clustering
- [`CVAA()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/CVAA.md)
  : Cumulative Voting Aggregation (CVAA / W-CVAA)
- [`ConsensusClustering()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/ConsensusClustering.md)
  : Voting-based consensus clustering
- [`EvidenceAccumulation()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/EvidenceAccumulation.md)
  : Evidence accumulation clustering (co-association)
- [`LinkBasedClustering()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/LinkBasedClustering.md)
  : Link-based cluster ensembles
- [`M_ABC()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/M_ABC.md)
  : Multi-source Aggregating Bundles of Clusters (M-ABC),
  C++-accelerated
- [`M_ABCdist()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/M_ABCdist.md)
  : Multi-source M-ABC with distance accumulation
- [`M_ABCdist.WC()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/M_ABCdist.WC.md)
  : Multi-source M-ABC fused with WeightedClust
- [`M_ABCdeep()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/M_ABCdeep.md)
  : Multi-source M-ABC with a deep-learning (autoencoder) Step 4
  (M-ABCdeep)
- [`ABCpp.SingleInMultiple()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/ABCpp.SingleInMultiple.md)
  : Single-source Aggregating Bundles of Clusters (ABC), C++-accelerated
  engine
- [`ABCdist.SingleInMultiple()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/ABCdist.SingleInMultiple.md)
  : Single-source ABC with distance accumulation
- [`ABCdeep.SingleInMultiple()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/ABCdeep.SingleInMultiple.md)
  : Single-source ABC with a deep-learning (autoencoder) Step 4
  (ABCdeep)
- [`f.clustABC.MultiSource()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/f.clustABC.MultiSource.md)
  : Consensus clustering from stacked ABC label matrices

## Integration — Hierarchy-based

Merge per-source hierarchies.

- [`HierarchicalEnsembleClustering()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/HierarchicalEnsembleClustering.md)
  : Hierarchical ensemble clustering
- [`EHC()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/EHC.md) :
  Ensemble hierarchical clustering via graph partitioning (METIS / MST)

## Additional methods (factor / low-rank / spectral)

Cluster a shared latent representation, or an outcome-guided model.

- [`intNMF()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/intNMF.md)
  : Integrative NMF clustering (intNMF)
- [`spectral_clustering()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/spectral_clustering.md)
  : Spectral clustering of an affinity matrix
- [`LUCID()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/LUCID.md)
  : LUCID: latent unknown clustering integrating omics with an outcome

## Feature weighting and data nuggets

Weight features by importance; compress objects into weighted
representatives.

- [`create_data_nuggets()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/create_data_nuggets.md)
  : Create data nuggets from a data matrix
- [`nugget_feature_weights()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/nugget_feature_weights.md)
  : Feature weights derived from data nuggets
- [`nugget_cluster()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/nugget_cluster.md)
  : Data-nugget clustering
- [`Wkmeans()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/Wkmeans.md)
  : Weighted k-means (minimises WWCSS)
- [`Whclust()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/Whclust.md)
  : Weighted hierarchical clustering (weighted Ward)
- [`DetermineWeight_SilClust()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/DetermineWeight_SilClust.md)
  : Determines an optimal weight for weighted clustering by silhouettes
  widths.
- [`DetermineWeight_SimClust()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/DetermineWeight_SimClust.md)
  : Determines an optimal weight for weighted clustering by similarity
  weighted clustering.
- [`simulate_weighting_regime()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/simulate_weighting_regime.md)
  : Simulate data for evaluating feature-weighting schemes (variance vs
  CV)

## Choosing the number of clusters

- [`SelectnrClusters()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/SelectnrClusters.md)
  : Select the number of clusters via silhouette widths
- [`ChooseCluster()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/ChooseCluster.md)
  : Interactive plot to determine DE Genes and DE features for a
  specific cluster
- [`cluster_selection_plot()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/cluster_selection_plot.md)
  : Justify the number of clusters (silhouette + elbow / scree)
- [`cluster_k_sweep()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/cluster_k_sweep.md)
  : Show the clustering at every k (see how it deteriorates)

## Label extraction and evaluation

Cut a result into clusters and score agreement, with or without ground
truth.

- [`mosaic_labels()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/mosaic_labels.md)
  : Extract a flat partition from a MosaiClusteR result
- [`cluster_agreement()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/cluster_agreement.md)
  : Agreement between two partitions
- [`compare_clusterings()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/compare_clusterings.md)
  : Compare two clusterings derived from distance matrices
- [`clustering_concordance()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/clustering_concordance.md)
  : Compare clustering solutions to each other (no ground truth needed)
- [`compare_methods_plot()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/compare_methods_plot.md)
  : Visually compare clustering solutions with ComparePlot (no ground
  truth)
- [`CompareSilCluster()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/CompareSilCluster.md)
  : Compares medoid clustering results based on silhouette widths
- [`CompareSvsM()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/CompareSvsM.md)
  : Comparison of clustering results for the single and multiple source
  clustering.

## Visualisation

- [`ComparePlot()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/ComparePlot.md)
  : Comparison of clustering results over multiple methods
- [`Cyclogram()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/Cyclogram.md)
  : Comparison of clustering results over multiple results in circular
  format
- [`ClusterPlot()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/ClusterPlot.md)
  : Colouring clusters in a dendrogram
- [`HeatmapPlot()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/HeatmapPlot.md)
  : A heatmap of the comparison of two clustering results.
- [`HeatmapSelection()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/HeatmapSelection.md)
  : A function to select a group of objects via the similarity heatmap.
- [`SimilarityHeatmap()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/SimilarityHeatmap.md)
  : A heatmap of similarity values between objects
- [`BoxPlotDistance()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/BoxPlotDistance.md)
  : Box plots of one distance matrix categorized against another
  distance matrix.
- [`ProfilePlot()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/ProfilePlot.md)
  : Plotting gene profiles
- [`embedding_plot()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/embedding_plot.md)
  : Two-dimensional cluster visualisation (PCA / UMAP / t-SNE)
- [`plot_cluster_profile()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/plot_cluster_profile.md)
  : Plot one external variable by cluster
- [`CompareInteractive()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/CompareInteractive.md)
  : Interactive comparison of single and multiple source clustering
  results
- [`ColorPalette()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/ColorPalette.md)
  : Create a color palette to be used in the plots
- [`ColorsNames()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/ColorsNames.md)
  : Function that annotates colors to their names
- [`ClusterCols()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/ClusterCols.md)
  : Helper that colours dendrogram leaves by cluster membership
- [`LabelCols()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/LabelCols.md)
  : Helper that colours specific dendrogram leaves
- [`LabelPlot()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/LabelPlot.md)
  : Coloring specific leaves of a dendrogram

## Cluster characterisation

Describe what defines each cluster, from external variables to features.

- [`characterize_clusters()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/characterize_clusters.md)
  : Characterise clusters with external (biological / clinical)
  variables
- [`cluster_biology_panel()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/cluster_biology_panel.md)
  : Panel of cluster characterisation plots
- [`CharacteristicFeatures()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/CharacteristicFeatures.md)
  : Determine the characteristic features of clusters
- [`FeatSelection()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/FeatSelection.md)
  : Determine the characteristic features of a cluster or selection
- [`FeaturesOfCluster()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/FeaturesOfCluster.md)
  : List all features present in a selected cluster of objects
- [`BinFeaturesPlot_SingleData()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/BinFeaturesPlot_SingleData.md)
  : Visualization of characteristic binary features of a single data set
- [`BinFeaturesPlot_MultipleData()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/BinFeaturesPlot_MultipleData.md)
  : Visualization of characteristic binary features of multiple data
  sets
- [`ContFeaturesPlot()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/ContFeaturesPlot.md)
  : Plot of continuous features
- [`TrackCluster()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/TrackCluster.md)
  : Track a cluster or a selection of objects across multiple methods

## Biological interpretation and pathways

Turn clusters into differential genes and enriched gene sets (needs
Bioconductor).

- [`DiffGenes()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/DiffGenes.md)
  : Find differentially expressed genes

- [`DiffGenesSelection()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/DiffGenesSelection.md)
  : Differential expression for a selection of objects

- [`FindGenes()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/FindGenes.md)
  : Find the genes shared across methods

- [`PathwayAnalysis()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/PathwayAnalysis.md)
  : Pathway analysis with intersection over iterations

- [`Pathways()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/Pathways.md)
  : Pathway analysis for multiple clustering results

- [`PathwaysIter()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/PathwaysIter.md)
  : Iterations of the pathway analysis

- [`PathwaysSelection()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/PathwaysSelection.md)
  : Pathway analysis for a selection of objects

- [`PreparePathway()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/PreparePathway.md)
  : Prepare data for pathway analysis

- [`PlotPathways()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/PlotPathways.md)
  : A GO plot of a pathway analysis output.

- [`plot_pathways()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/plot_pathways.md)
  : Modern Gene Ontology / pathway-enrichment plots

- [`enriched_features()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/enriched_features.md)
  : Tidy CharacteristicFeatures() output for plotting

- [`Geneset.intersect()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/Geneset.intersect.md)
  :

  Intersection over resulting gene sets of `PathwaysIter` function

- [`Geneset.intersectSelection()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/Geneset.intersectSelection.md)
  :

  Intersection over resulting gene sets of `PathwaysIter` function for a
  selection of objects

- [`SharedGenesPathsFeat()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/SharedGenesPathsFeat.md)
  : Shared genes, pathways and features across methods

- [`SharedComps()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/SharedComps.md)
  : Objects shared across clusterings

- [`SharedSelection()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/SharedSelection.md)
  : Intersection of genes and pathways over multiple methods for a
  selection of objects.

- [`SharedSelectionLimma()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/SharedSelectionLimma.md)
  : Intersection of genes over multiple methods for a selection of
  objects.

- [`SharedSelectionMLP()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/SharedSelectionMLP.md)
  : Intersection of pathways over multiple methods for a selection of
  objects.

## Simulation and data

- [`mosaic_sim()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/mosaic_sim.md)
  : Simulate a multi-source data set with planted clusters
- [`mosaic_toy`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/mosaic_toy.md)
  : Toy multi-omics example data

## Utilities

- [`ReorderToReference()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/ReorderToReference.md)
  : Relabel and reorder clusterings to a reference

- [`FindCluster()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/FindCluster.md)
  :

  Find a selection of objects in the output of `ReorderToReference`

- [`FindElement()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/FindElement.md)
  : Find an element in a data structure

- [`Distance()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/Distance.md)
  [`Distance_v2()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/Distance.md)
  : Compute a distance matrix

- [`distanceheatmaps()`](https://lucp12891.github.io/MosaiClusteR/reference/distanceheatmaps.md)
  : Determine the distance in a heatmap
